content.title: Celtics-Magic recap: ‘Stay Ready' C's win wild regular-season finale
content.text: What to KnowChris Forsberg and Kayla Burton shared more postgame reaction on the Celtics Talk Podcast.Celtics beat the fully healthy Magic without eight key players.Baylor Scheierman (30 points, 6-14 3-PT) and Ron Harper Jr. (27 points, 5-12 3-PT) scored career-highs.Luka Garza added 27 points (3-6 3-PT) and 12 rebounds.Boston will play winner of No. 7 Sixers vs. No. 8 Magic in Round 1 of playoffs. The Boston Celtics' B Team stunned the fully healthy Orlando Magic in Sunday's regular-season finale at TD Garden, 113-108. Check out our live blog below for a full recap of Sunday's game: The Boston Celtics' bench crew took down a fully healthy Orlando Magic squad in Sunday's regular-season finale at TD Garden, 113-108. With the No. 2 seed already locked up, the Celtics rested eight rotation players -- including all five starters -- for Sunday's game. The Magic, on the other hand, needed to win to earn the No. 7 seed and host their play-in tournament matchup. Boston trailed by 11 points in the second quarter, but it turned that deficit into a 16-point lead during a thoroughly dominant third. The C's outscored the Magic 42-20 in the frame. Orlando stormed back and tied it with a Jalen Suggs 3-pointer with 35 seconds left in the fourth, but Celtics big man Luka Garza answered with a 3 of his own. Boston's B Team held on from there to escape with a hard-fought victory, forcing the Magic to play on the road against the Philadelphia 76ers in their play-in showdown. The Celtics won't know their first round opponent until Wednesday night, but they know when their postseason journey begins. The NBA has announced that Game 1 of Boston's first-round series will be on Sunday, April 19 at 1 p.m. ET. Luka Garza appeared to go rogue on his dagger 3-pointer, catching the inbound pass and drilling a contested deep ball with 31.6 seconds left. It may not have been exactly the play Joe Mazzulla drew up, but teammate Baylor Scheierman loved it: The Celtics were without eight rotation players, but TD Garden kept the same energy Sunday night, going wild in the fourth quarter as Boston's bench crew fended off the Magic for the victory. Head coach Joe Mazzulla wasn't surprised to see the fans so engaged in the game despite the circumstances. "The great thing about our fans is they're smart," Mazzulla said. "They know good basketball. They care about winning." Eddie House and our Celtics Postgame Live crew react after Boston's bench STUNNED the Magic in Sunday's regular-season finale: Our Postgame Live crew reacts to the Celtics’ incredible win over the Orlando Magic. Baylor Scheierman caught up with NBC Sports Boston's Abby Chin after dropping a career-high 30 points in Sunday's season finale win over Orlando: Abby Chin talks with Baylor Scheierman after the Celtics' improbable win over the Orlando Magic Abby Chin talks with Baylor Scheierman after the Celtics’ improbable win over the Orlando Magic The No. 2 seed Boston Celtics will await the winner of the Orlando Magic-Philadelphia 76ers play-in matchup in the first round of the NBA playoffs. Boston defeated Orlando 113-108 in Sunday's regular-season finale to force the Magic to face Philly on the road. The Sixers beat the Milwaukee Bucks 126-106 in their final game of the campaign. Here's how the Eastern Conference looks ahead of the play-in tournament, plus dates and times for C's fans to mark on their calendars: Boston will take on either Orlando or Philadelphia in the first round of the NBA playoffs. The Magic will visit the 76ers in a play-in battle for the No. 7 seed. Read Full Article The Celtics will meet either the Magic or the 76ers in Round 1 of the NBA playoffs. Orlando and Philly will face off for the No. 7 seed on Wednesday night at 7:30 p.m. ET. Check out the full playoff picture below: Score: 111-108 Celtics, 31.6 seconds left in the fourth quarter Right after Jalen Suggs hit the game-tying 3 for Orlando, Luka Garza drilled a 3 of his own to put Boston back ahead. Score: 108-108, 34.8 seconds left in fourth quarter Jalen Suggs hit a game-tying 3-pointer with 35 seconds remaining. The Magic are on a 9-0 run. Score: 108-104 Celtics, 1:37 left in fourth quarter The Magic are making it interesting late in the fourth as they've cut the Celtics' lead to four. Desmond Bane drilled a clutch 3-pointer to help keep Orlando alive. Score: 104-99 Celtics, 4:21 left in fourth quarter After the Celtics' dominant fourth quarter, the Magic have answered with a strong start to the fourth. They've outscored Boston 18-10 so far in the frame to trim the deficit to five with just over four minutes to play. Ron Harper Jr. (27 points) exited the game with an apparent injury and is being worked on by trainers on the C's bench. Score: 101-88 Celtics, 8:16 left in fourth quarter Baylor Scheierman has reached the 30-point mark for the first time in his career. The Celtics sharpshooter is 8-of-16 from the floor, including 6-of-11 from 3-point range. He and Ron Harper Jr. (27 points) have been the stars tonight for the C's. Luka Garza has also been exceptional with 20 points and 10 rebounds. Score: 94-81 Celtics The Celtics' second team outscored the fully healthy Magic 42-20 in the third quarter to turn an 11-point deficit into a 13-point lead. Baylor Scheierman (28 points) and Ron Harper Jr. (27 points) have put on a show for the "Stay Ready" C's. The duo has combined to shoot 11-for-23 from 3-point range. Luka Garza has also had a big night with 20 points (7-13 FG) and 10 rebounds. Franz Wagner leads the Magic with 20 points. Score: 77-73 Celtics, 4:19 left in third quarter The Celtics' "Stay Ready Group" is on fire in the third quarter. Boston erased an 11-point deficit and now leads by four. It has outscored Orlando 25-12 in the frame. Ron Harper Jr. (24 points, 9-17 FG) and Baylor Scheierman (22 points, 6-14 FG) have been outstanding for the C's. They've combined for eight 3-pointers. Luka Garza has 14 points and 10 rebounds. Score: 71-67 Magic, 6:47 left in third quarter The Celtics have cut the deficit to four by outscoring the Magic 15-10 so far in the third quarter. Baylor Scheierman, Jordan Walsh, and Max Shulga each made 3s for the C's in the frame. Shulga's 3 was the first of his career. Scheierman and Ron Harper Jr. lead Boston with 19 points apiece. Scheierman appeared to tweak his back, but he's staying in the game. Score: 61-52 Magic The Celtics trail at the half, but they're still within striking distance of the Magic despite missing eight of their key players. Ron Harper Jr. has made the most of his opportunity for the C's. He leads all scorers with 17 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3-PT). Baylor Scheierman (14 points) and Luka Garza (12 points) have also made an impact, but it hasn't been a very efficient night so far for Boston. The Celtics are shooting just 33 percent from the floor, including 7-of-25 (28 percent) from 3-point range. Score: 51-43 Magic, 3:21 left in second quarter Three of the Celtics' starters (Luka Gaeza, Ron Harper Jr., Baylor Scheierman) are in double figures, but Boston is shooting just 33 percent from the floor. Score: 37-32 Magic, 8:43 left in second quarter Baylor Scheierman has seven of the Celtics' 12 points so far in the second and 10 points altogether. John Tonje added a 3-pointer to cut the deficit to five. Ron Harper Jr. and Franz Wagner are tied for a game-high 12 points each. Score: 29-20 Magic The Celtics' second team will have to mount a comeback as the Magic, who are playing at full strength, will take an nine-point lead into the second quarter. Boston is without eight key players to rest them up for the playoffs. Ron Harper Jr. stepped up for the C's in the opening frame with 12 of the team's 20 points on 4-of-7 shooting. Luka Garza and Baylor Scheierman chipped in with a 3-pointer apiece. Franz Wagner leads the Magic with eight points. Orlando is shooting 42 percent from the floor (5-13 3-PT), while Boston is shooting just 26 percent (4-16 3PT). Score: 23-18 Magic, 2:25 left in first quarter Ron Harper Jr. has scored 10 of the Celtics' 18 points on 4-of-6 shooting, including a pair of 3-pointers: Jalen Suggs and Franz Wagner have helped keep the Magic ahead with six points apiece. Orlando is shooting 45 percent from the floor to Boston's 32 percent. Score: 10-8 Celtics, 7:59 left in first quarter Luka Garza and Baylor Scheierman drilled 3-pointers for the C's before Ron Harper Jr. came through with a quick four points to put Boston ahead. Franz Wagner has a team-high six points for the Magic. Boston is shooting 4-of-11 from the floor (2-7 3-PT), while Orlando is 3-for-8 (2-4 3-PT) through the first four minutes. Tonight, we're celebrating the historic career of Jim Edmonds, who has been the Celtics game broadcast director since 1981. Thank you, Jim, for 45 years.
